Six figures the brief treats as fact are not reproducible from any file at the base commit: '254 rows' and '279 rows' for the Week 10 tables, '4 no-injury sections vs 2', '6 of 254 report rows carry a game designation', '149 club/unit/position slots with more than one rank-1 player', and 'the 136-ga

No official source publishes a market price. Every requirement that depends on a price (opening/closing snapshots, the difference column, the residual, CLV, vig decomposition, ROI, rewards) is blocked by the same missing input, and the sibling workspaces in this repository have each worked around it

The W-L record printed in brackets beside each club on the injury report is a live join, not a pre-game attribute: it equalled the LIVE standings for 28 of 28 clubs at read time, including clubs whose games were still in progress and clubs that had not kicked off.

The depth-requirement family (rank-1 groups, shared and empty slots, the Texans image, the Packers jersey-prefix, the 1st-4th string matrix) presumes a depth dataset that exists in neither this repo nor on nfl.com; peers recorded the nfl.com team depth-chart route as a 404.

The brief cites dated starter changes for Lock, McCord and Brissett (VR-24, VR-25; VQ-05). Lock and McCord were located in official text this session; the Brissett item was not, and none of the VR/VQ identifiers exist in any file at the base commit.

'Publish the league's dated schedule announcement beside the live schedule page': no official nfl.com schedule-release article with a printed date was located this session; a web search returned only third-party reposts of the release video.
At read time three Week 10 games were still in progress on the schedule page (Q4, Q4, Q3) while the live standings already credited them; two others had not kicked off.
Four clubs have no section in the Week 10 report (CHI, DEN, PHI, TB). Reading an absent section as 'no injuries' is wrong: the schedule page's own 'Teams on Bye' block lists exactly those four.

A traded player still appears on his former club's official report: Daiyan Henley is listed on the Chargers' Week 10 report (LB, full participation) five days after the roundup records both clubs announcing the trade to Denver.

The report's Injuries column is not a severity source: Puka Nacua's row leaves it blank while a dated official item says IR with turf toe and sprained MCL/PCL, and eight Giants players have injuries named in Tuesday's official practice text but blank injury cells in the report.

Non-injury reasons are published inside the Injuries column: 'Not injury related - resting player' (JAX x2, LAR x1) and 'Not injury related - personal matter' (HOU x1, LAC x1). Any feature counting injury labels counts a rest day as an injury.

Position labels on the official report are not verified against a roster source: one row reads 'Patrick O'Connell, LB' for Seattle, a player publicly known as a quarterback; it cannot be determined from the pages read whether this is a publication error or a reclassification.
Six dated captures of one official page sit in this repo with row counts 347, 347, 326, 326, 276 and 107. Five of the six are strict subsets of the fullest capture; two agree exactly.

This session's own first parse put practice-status text into the game-status column for 5 rows (an extra comma on blank-injury rows). It was caught only by diffing against an independent peer capture of the same page, not by the parse itself.

Capture is a transcription of a rendered page, not of page bytes: hashes in data/capture_manifest.json cover the transcription, and the fetch window is bracketed between two known clock readings because the harness exposes no per-call time.

The report page is rolling: the week control offers WEEK 1..WEEK 10 for 2026, so past weeks may be reachable - but this session did not test whether selecting an earlier week returns that week's report or the current one.

Several namespaces in one repository answer the same brief in parallel, and at least four of them publish a decision-readiness or requirements register with different row counts and different verdicts for the same requirement.
